finding: The model does not beat the majority-class baseline (ROC-AUC ~0.5, essentially random). Every (sender, recipient) pair in the dataset appears exactly once (0 repeated pairs across 372 labeled interactions) -- there is no repeated co-occurrence signal for user embeddings to learn from. This is a genuine data-sparsity finding, not an implementation bug: v1 (no regularization) confirmed the model can fit training data to near-zero loss, so it has the capacity to learn -- it simply has nothing generalizable to learn from this interaction volume. This empirically validates the live app's hybrid.js design, which deliberately weights content-based similarity (alpha=0.9) over collaborative signal when accepted-interaction counts are low.
